meta.title: Welfare and public spending
meta.question: Should the state provide more, or should taxes be lower?
meta.measure: Average position on public services and benefits, from 0 (more public services and benefits) to 10 (lower taxes and self-reliance)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on the state's responsibility for the old, the sick and the unemployed, on spending on pensions, benefits and health care, and on taxes against spending, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

Should it be the government's responsibility to provide health care for the sick?

items.notes: WVS 1997, 2005, 2012 (3). WVS 1989 puts the ends the other way round: WVS_GOVRESP_1989. Directions confirmed by the items' correlations with ownership and income equality.

items.wording: There should be more spending on social welfare (agree-disagree)
items.notes: CCEB 2002.1 (March 2002); codes run from 1 strongly disagree to 5 strongly agree. Correlates 0.66 with CCEB_INCDIFF_TOO_WIDE.

items.wording: It is the responsibility of the state to take care of very poor people who can't take care of themselves (completely agree ... completely disagree)
items.notes: Pew 2002 and 2007. Very consensual (over 90% agree) and unrelated to the free-market question in both surveys.

items.wording: Should the government decrease taxes a lot and spend much less on social benefits and services (0), or increase them a lot (10)?

Social benefits and services place too great a strain on the economy (agree-disagree)

What is more important: that everyone be free to pursue their life's goals without interference from the state, or that the state play an active role in society so as to guarantee that nobody is in need?
